messages:
Maya Chen: Thanks for the all-hands — quick Q: on the loss patterns you called out, can leadership share the top 3 reasons we're losing deals and which of those are product/roadmap vs sales/ops?
Samir Patel: From sales notes: 1) compliance/security (SOC2, data residency) 2) pricing/commit length (esp for mid-market) 3) perf & model fidelity vs customer-tuned alternatives. Mostly a combo: 1 is product+biz, 2 is GTM, 3 is product.
Dylan K: On the product side we see two clear engineering themes: latency/cost at scale (customers hit token budgets) and quality regressions when comparing to competitor fine-tunes. Both need infra+model work.
Leah O'Neill: From CS: a bunch of losses were about onboarding friction for Private (VPC/on-prem). Customers need a "day 1" runbook and a checklist for security teams. That feels more ops than core model work.
Rajiv Menon: We're prioritizing triage items: SOC2 & formal attestations, Dedicated pricing revisions, and Private onboarding docs. Requesting input: which of these moves the needle fastest for renewals/new deals?
Maya Chen: Can we get a % split on ARR impacted by each reason? Even rough numbers will help prioritize.
Samir Patel: Rough ballpark from last quarter rep notes: compliance/security ~40% of lost/paused deals, pricing/commit issues ~30%, perf/quality ~30%. Caveat: sampling bias toward enterprise leads.
Anna Lopez: Helpful — thanks. Suggest we treat SOC2 + Private onboarding as highest immediate blocker for enterprise expansion, then Dedicated pricing for mid-market.
Dylan K: @Maya I'll put together a short perf appendix with numbers and tail-latency breakdowns. Preview: p50~40ms, p95~220ms on standard configs; customers hitting p95 spikes during long-context workloads. Link to internal benchmark: https://redwood.internal/bench/perf-q1 :link:
Leah O'Neill: Quick note — some CS teams report customers asking for model pinning/custom fine-tunes as a tie-breaker. That's product but also services.
Rajiv Menon: For roadmap clarity: SOC2 compliance effort scheduled for Q2 (security sprint), Private onboarding docs + runbooks are a top infra short task (can be done in weeks), Dedicated pricing overhaul targeted Q3. We'll publish a timeline and owners.
Maya Chen: Can we get owners + a one-line acceptance criteria per item? Eg SOC2 = external audit complete; Private onboarding = step-by-step deploy guide + 2 verified customer installs; Pricing = new mid-market SKUs live.
Anna Lopez: Agreed. Owners: @Rajiv for SOC2 (with Security), @Dylan for perf work and model pinning feasibility, @Leah for Private onboarding validation, @Samir for pricing experiments.
Samir Patel: I'll run two A/B experiments for pricing (12mo commit vs usage cap) and report conversion delta.
Dylan K: I'll share the perf appendix and a short RFC for "model pinning" options (pin+quantized variants vs custom fine-tune offering).
ops-bot: All-hands recording uploaded: https://redwood.internal/records/allhands-2026-03-22. Meeting notes doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/allhands-2026-03-22
Maya Chen: Awesome — can we reconvene in 2 weeks with owners' one-liners and any quant? I'll synthesize for the next planning sync. :thumbsup:
Leah O'Neill: +1, will validate onboarding checklist with 2 customers this week and report back.
Rajiv Menon: I'll add SOC2 milestones to the public roadmap page and tag owners.
Anna Lopez: Thanks everyone — this is exactly the actionable follow-up we wanted from the all-hands.
Samir Patel: Thanks — will share preliminary pricing results within 10 business days.
Dylan K: Uploading perf appendix shortly.
Maya Chen: Closing the loop here — feel free to ping me with blockers.
